sections.heading: C — Your driving privilege: license points, suspensions, revocations, hearings, unpaid fines and restoration (North Carolina)
sections.markdown:
## C — Your driving privilege: license points, suspensions, revocations, hearings, unpaid fines and restoration (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: how North Carolina adds license points for convictions, when points or specific offenses cost you the license, how to challenge or avoid a suspension, and how to get the license back.

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
Being convicted of certain motor vehicle violations in North Carolina puts driver license points on your driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Once you reach seven points, DMV may send you to a driver improvement clinic, and the clinic costs $83.50. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Finishing the driver improvement clinic satisfactorily takes three points off your record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Collecting 12 points within three years can get your license suspended. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
After your license is reinstated, gathering eight points within the next three years can bring a second suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
A point-system suspension lasts 60 days the first time, six months the second time and 12 months the third time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
When your privilege is reinstated, every earlier driver license point is wiped out, but insurance points are not affected. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
In a regular vehicle, passing a stopped school bus and aggressive driving each carry 5 points, the highest values on the regular schedule. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Illegal passing, reckless driving, tailgating (following too closely), a property-damage-only hit and run, and driving on the wrong side of the road each carry 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield to a pedestrian under the cited statute, or to a bicycle, motor scooter or motorcycle, carries 4 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A01
Running a stop sign, running a red light, failing to yield right of way, and speeding faster than 55 mph each carry 3 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A01
Driving with no license or one expired over a year, ignoring a siren, driving through a safety zone, and having no liability insurance each carry 3 points. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
Failing to file a required accident report and speeding above a posted school zone limit each carry 3 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
Not properly restraining a child in a child restraint or seat belt carries 2 points, the same as any other moving violation not listed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
Littering that involves the use of a motor vehicle carries 1 point. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
While operating a commercial motor vehicle, passing a stopped school bus carries 8 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
In a commercial motor vehicle, a rail-highway crossing violation and aggressive driving each carry 6 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A02
In a commercial motor vehicle, reckless driving carries 5 points, running a red light 4 points and any other moving violation 3 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A02
Having an alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle carries 4 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A03
Overload, overlength, overwidth and overheight convictions add no points, and neither does illegal parking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A03
Plate, registration, muffler, emblem and inspection-certificate offenses, and carrying a concealed weapon, add no points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A03
A point-carrying offense committed in a commercial motor vehicle may be charged double any fine or penalty the statute authorizes. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A03
Insurance companies set rates with their own separate point system, and your insurance agent can answer questions about it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A03
On top of any criminal penalty from the court, conviction of certain traffic offenses takes away your driving privilege. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A03
DMV can suspend your license for two over-55 mph speeding convictions within 12 months, or one over-55 speeding conviction plus one reckless driving conviction within a year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A03
A conviction for willful racing against another vehicle, planned ahead or not, lets DMV suspend your license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A03
DMV can also suspend when a court sentence orders you not to drive for a set time, and in certain cases after a conviction for speeding over 75 mph. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A03
Driving more than 15 mph over the limit while going faster than 55 mph brings a revocation of at least 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A03
The revocation is 60 days for a second over-55, more-than-15-over speeding charge within one year, or for speeding together with reckless driving on the same occasion. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A04
DMV may suspend your privilege as soon as it receives the conviction report from the court, and a revoked driver may have a right to a hearing in the judicial district where they live. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A04
To ask for a hearing you call 919-715-7000 or use Contact Us on NCDMV.gov, and DMV mails you the hearing time and place. [A04]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; phone number and web contact can change.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A04
If the hearing does not help, you may appeal the DMV decision within 30 days to the Superior Court of your home county. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A04
Manslaughter, death by vehicle and assault with a motor vehicle each bring a one-year suspension, while manslaughter while impaired brings a permanent one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A04
Failing to stop and give aid after a crash, and willfully refusing a blood or breath alcohol test, each bring a one-year suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A04
Speeding over 55 mph and at least 15 mph over the limit while trying to avoid arrest brings a one-year suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A04
Two reckless driving charges within 12 months, or trying to get a license or learner permit under false pretenses, each bring a one-year suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A04
Prearranged highway racing, and watching, betting on or lending a car for it, carry a three-year suspension, and the officer seizes the car, which a court may order sold at public auction after conviction. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A04
Failing to yield in the listed situations, such as entering an intersection or at a highway construction or maintenance area, when the offense causes serious bodily injury brings 90 days and $500. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A05
A conviction in another state can lead to suspension or revocation of your North Carolina license as though it happened here, and DMV must notify you in writing of the effective date. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A05
If you miss court or do not pay a fine for a citation, DMV sets a revocation date that takes effect unless the fine is paid or waived first, and it lasts until the court reports payment or waiver. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F41 | anchor: A05
Taking care of the citation does not cancel the consequences of the offense itself if you are convicted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F42 | anchor: A05
If you cannot afford a ticket, you file the Motion for Relief form with the clerk in the county where you got the ticket and ask for a hearing, where the judge may lower the amount, set a payment plan or waive it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F43 | anchor: A05
If you can pay in full, you contact the clerk in that county, pay the whole amount, and the court tells DMV, which stops the suspension. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-F44 | anchor: A06
A provisional licensee under 18 faces a 30-day suspension for a second moving violation conviction within 12 months. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-F45 | anchor: A06
A provisional licensee faces 90 days for a third and six months for a fourth moving violation conviction within 12 months. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-F46 | anchor: A06
Clearing a suspension or revocation requires a restoration fee of $83.50, except when the license was taken for medical reasons after a medical evaluation. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-F47 | anchor: A06
Restoring after a DWI revocation costs $167.25, and a $50 service fee also applies unless you surrendered the license to the court or mailed it to DMV before the effective date. [A06]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; fees can change.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-F48 | anchor: A06
To get your privilege back you go to a driver license office, prove identity, pay the fees, reapply, take any required tests, show insurance if required and pay for the new license. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

Misconceptions: license points and insurance points are separate systems, so reinstatement clears only license points; a point-system suspension is not the only route to losing a license, because many single offenses carry their own suspension; paying or contesting a ticket does not erase the offense; commercial drivers carry higher point values for the same act.
Mnemonics: clinic, then suspension, then a lower bar after reinstatement; for under-eighteen drivers the count is second, third, fourth violation inside one year.
Glossary: points means values added to a driving record on conviction; suspension and revocation mean loss of the driving privilege for a period; restoration fee means the charge to clear a suspension; provisional licensee means a driver under eighteen; Motion for Relief means the court form asking to reduce or waive a fine.
Dynamic facts: fees, the hearing phone line and web payment options can change and are flagged as dynamic; confirm on the NCDMV and court websites.
